'''John Edward McCosker''' is an American [[ichthyologist]] and as has been part of expeditions to many countries such as [[Antarctica]], [[Australia]], and the [[Galápagos Islands|Galapagos]]. After extensive study and ten expeditions he is one of the foremost experts on the Galapagos. He has been featured in various different television documentaries as well as working with filmmakers and other documentary programs off screen.

McCosker earned his [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] degree from the [[Occidental College]] (Los Angeles) in 1967. He attended the [[Scripps Institution of Oceanography]] in 1973 where McCosker gained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree. Currently he is a senior scientist at the [[California Academy of Sciences]] based in San Francisco. He joined the academy in 1973 as superintendent within the [[Steinhart Aquarium]]. Between 1976 and 1994 he was the director. From 1988 to 1989, and again in 1995, he was the Interim Executive Director for the Academy.

The [[genus|generic name]] of the [[blenny]] ''[[Mccoskerichthys sandae]]'' honours McCosker, because he discovered it and assisted in the collection of the [[Type (biology)|type]] while its [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]] honours his then wife, Sandra.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.etyfish.org/blenniiformes3/ | title = Order BLENNIIFORMES: Families CLINIDAE, LABRISOMIDAE and CHAENOPSIDAE | work = ETYFish Fish Name Etymology Database | author1 = Christopher Scharpf | author2 = Kenneth J. Lazara | publisher = Christopher Scharpf and Kenneth J. Lazara | date = 10 November 2018 | access-date = 15 April 2019}}</ref>

Dr. McCosker also appeared on The Tonight Show, starring Johnny Carson on July 12, 1984. Other guests on the episode were Miss Piggy and Howie Mandel.
